runs.name: Enel Chile S.A.; NYSE ENIC, ADSs of 50 shares of common stock, SEC CIK 0001659939, Chile, 20-F filer; generation and distribution of electricity in Chile through subsidiaries, 8,904 MW net installed capacity and about 2.2 million distribution customers at 2025-12-31; Enel beneficially owns 64.93%; formed 2016 as Enersis Chile in the Enersis split, renamed October 2016; functional and presentation currency changed from Chilean pesos to US dollars effective 2025-01-01; the 20-F names Colbun, Engie Energia Chile, GM Holdings and AES Andes, none an SEC filer, AES Corp's Chilean segment used as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **US$4.34** per ADS (close 2026-10-22, aggregator, flagged), US$0.0868 per share. Shares **69,166,557,219**, one class (20-F cover, 0001104659-26-050251; no treasury shares, no purchases in 2025, no issuance in the 6-Ks since), 1,383.33M ADS equivalents; market cap US$6,003.7M; net debt US$3,509M at 2026-06-30 (about US$1.03bn of it lent by Enel Finance International). Sovereign **5.29%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-22: the earnings currency judged the dollar from the 20-F's own functional-currency reasoning (generation's dollar-linked contracts); a Chilean peso sovereign from the Banco Central de Chile not obtained, confessed, no figure depends on it. Read from the 20-F FY2025 (0001104659-26-050251) and the 20-Fs FY2017 to FY2024, the Q1 and Q2 2026 interim statements on 6-K (0001292814-26-002712, 0001292814-26-003952) and the material-fact 6-K of 2026-04-29; no proxy (foreign private issuer); lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 20-F's Items 4, 3.D and 5; pre-2025 peso years translated at the Banco Central de Chile annual average and the 20-F year-end rates, the company's own method, a CONVENTION of the run. Run from scratch by one dispatched analyst. **Q1 IN**: the economics read from the figures; price, rainfall and policy routed by the text to Q2, Q7 and Q9. **Q2 OUT**: the deciding part is Generation, 92.9% of the two segments' 2021 to 2025 operating income, selling a commodity through price-only auctions and a spot market where the marginal plant sets the price; operating income after a 27% statutory tax (a CONVENTION of the run) over equity plus net debt ran 6.5%, -0.4%, 3.2%, 9.1%, 7.4%, 3.2% and 8.2% in 2019 to 2025, about 5% as filed and about 7% with the 2020 Bocamina II impairment and the 2024 US$657M hedge-discontinuation loss added back; regulated sales fell from 13,895 to 10,616 GWh in 2025 at "a lower average sales price"; three tariff-stabilization laws made the generators finance customers' bills; the rival on the SEC record (AES Corp's Chilean segment, a CONVENTION of the run) earned 7.1% to 11.0% before overhead in 2015 to 2020 and then wrote off US$781M (2020), US$644M of goodwill (2022) and US$137M (2023), with Alto Maipo through Chapter 11; the regulated return the text allows as an exception belongs to distribution, which does not decide; no change for the better shown. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the SEF fines of about US$20M (August 2024 storm outages) and about US$8.5M (2025) against Enel Distribucion Chile, the US$17.1M SERNAC compensation, SERNAC guilty verdicts under appeal, the 2016 GasAtacama fine for allegedly erroneous information (reduced on appeal 2019). COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash after all spending, leases and minority dividends **US$223.4M a year 2021 to 2025** (US$39.1M after interest), swinging -528 (2021) to 875 (2024) with the stabilization receivables built and sold; maintenance-only cycle base US$700.2M (2019 to 2024, depreciation as the maintenance guess; US$711.4M with 2018); value range **US$5.38 to US$7.03 per ADS** all-equity against US$4.34, growth capped at the 1.39% sales growth, the bought growth worth less than its cost so the no-growth case the top; no case earns the floor at the price (best 7.36%, 8.58% equity-only); fair price **US$1.65 per ADS all-equity**, US$2.79 equity-only beside; the regulated-utility basis judged not to govern, the deciding part being priced by a market. After the stop, facts recorded, not weighed: capital spending US$499M to US$1,075M a year against depreciation of US$273M to US$387M while output went 21,041 to 21,583 GWh and 636 MW of coal closed; Los Condores about US$1.2bn for 153 MW; receivables about 30% of revenue (2019) to 63% (2024); goodwill near Ch$0.9 trillion since 2016; the CNE's 2025 methodological error over-billing regulated customers. Commits be4a1d67 (template), 79b84dcf (Step 0), af80bf75 (Q2 OUT), 384cf6af (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared: before reading the blind rule the analyst listed `Test Runs/` filtered for ENIC, Enel and Enersis (no file printed), the EDN fold's commit subjects and memory index lines; none used. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 27 adjacent quoted fragments, 1 flagged and read (a 20-F quotation on the line before **[M2006-004]**, not set beside it as the row's words), **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q7(c)'s "net of businesses sold" would credit the 2022 transmission-sale proceeds as owner cash, left out with the tax on the gains added back; (2) no rule for working capital that is a loan the regulator forces on the company, which here sets the whole cycle; (3) the maintenance-only case assumes spending above depreciation buys growth, much of it here replacing closed coal plants; (4) whether the regulated part's debt is credited on the equity-only figure of a mixed business; (5) the rival rule assumes a named rival files with the SEC. Could not get: the Chilean peso long-bond sovereign from the issuing authority; the rivals' cost per MWh; a generation maintenance capital figure (only distribution's US$43.6M disclosed); the 2016 to 2018 statements beyond a few lines. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Enel Chile, ENIC; electricity generation and distribution in Chile, 20-F filer, Enel 64.93%; the deciding part, Generation at 92.9% of segment operating income, sells a commodity at the low bid and at the marginal plant's price, and the company and the one rival on the SEC record earned ordinary returns over 2019 to 2025, about 5% after tax on capital as filed, about 7% adjusted; three tariff laws made the generators finance customers' bills; integrity facts recorded, not judged; computation only: owner cash US$223.4M a year 2021 to 2025, value range US$5.38 to US$7.03 per ADS vs US$4.34, no case earns the floor, fair US$1.65 all-equity, US$2.79 equity-only; peso sovereign not obtained, confessed; named rivals none an SEC filer; no citation slip; not held; not armed; framework gaps for the operator: divestiture proceeds under Q7(c), regulator-forced working capital, maintenance spending that replaces closed plants, the utility debt credit in a mixed business, the rival rule with no SEC-filing rival)
